w: Domingos Bongestabs built this 2,400-seat theatre from steel tubes in just 75 days, setting it in the middle of an artificial lake inside a former rock quarry and reaching it only by a walkway. Opened on 18 March 1992, the 360-tonne structure is now one of Curitiba's signature tourist sights.
s: A 360-tonne opera house made of wire
_facts: Also known as the Opera de Arame; a 2,400-seat theatre built from steel tubes
Weighs 360 tons of steel; designed by Domingos Bongestabs; built in 75 days
Set in an artificial lake on the site of a former rock quarry, reached by a walkway
Opened 18 March 1992; part of the Parque das Pedreiras (Park of the Quarries)

w: Established in 1991 as a French formal garden, the park's main greenhouse spans 458 square metres of Art Nouveau ironwork deliberately echoing London's Crystal Palace. Next door, a museum devoted to Polish-Brazilian artist Franz Krajcberg occupies 1,320 square metres among the fountains and lakes.
s: A Crystal Palace echo in a French garden
_facts: Formally Jardim Botanico Fanchette Rischbieter; established 1991 in French formal garden style
Main greenhouse spans 458 square metres, built in Art Nouveau style resembling London's Crystal Palace
Park covers 240,000 square metres, with fountains, waterfalls and lakes
Includes the Botanic Museum and, adjacent to the greenhouse, a 1,320-square-metre museum devoted to artist Franz Krajcberg

w: Built to honour the Japanese immigrants who began arriving in Parana in 1910, this square marks a community that put down deep roots: as of 2023, more than 32,000 of their descendants live in the state, the second-largest Japanese population in Brazil after Sao Paulo.
s: A square for Parana's Japanese settlers
_facts: Built in honour of Japanese immigrants who began arriving in Brazil from 1910
Parana has the second-largest Japanese community in Brazil, behind Sao Paulo
As of 2023, home to more than 32,000 descendants of Japanese immigrants

w: Once a municipal rock quarry, this 25,000-capacity outdoor venue is ringed by a 30-metre rock wall and named partly for poet Paulo Leminski. Neighbours' noise complaints shut it down under a 2008 court injunction; a renovation costing R$17 million reopened it in March 2014.
_facts: 25,000-capacity outdoor concert venue, formerly the municipal rock quarry, in the Abranches neighbourhood
Partly named after 20th-century Brazilian writer Paulo Leminski; opened 1990
Surrounded by a 30-metre-high rock wall; the Wire Opera House opened alongside it in 1992
Closed by court injunction in 2008 over noise complaints; reopened in March 2014 after a R$17 million renovation

w: Laid out in 1996 to honour Curitiba's early-19th-century German settlers, this park sends visitors down a trail to a gingerbread and candy house lifted straight from Hansel and Gretel. On Saturday afternoons, a storyteller still recounts the Brothers Grimm tale for children there.
s: A woodland trail to a gingerbread house
_facts: German Wood park, built to honour German immigrants who began settling in Curitiba in the early 19th century
Features a Hansel and Gretel trail leading to a gingerbread and candy house
A storyteller tells the Brothers Grimm tale to children, usually on Saturday afternoons
Inaugurated 13 April 1996

n: Museu de Historia Natural Capao da Imbuia
w: Run by Curitiba's Municipal Environment Secretariat, this natural history museum sits inside a remnant patch of Araucaria forest in the Capao da Imbuia district. Its research and scientific collections focus specifically on the fauna of Parana state, alongside conservation and environmental education work.
s: A natural history museum in an Araucaria forest
_facts: A division of the Department of Research and Conservation of Fauna, Municipal Environment Secretariat of Curitiba
Located in the Capao da Imbuia neighbourhood, in an area of remnant Araucaria forest
Conducts zoological research, conservation and environmental education, with scientific collections on Parana's fauna

w: Brazil's only Egyptian mummy, Tothmea, rests here - donated in 1995 by the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum of San Jose, California. The rest of the collection is mostly replicas spanning several pharaonic periods, gathered since the museum opened on 17 October 1990.
_facts: Egyptian archaeology museum in Curitiba, opened 17 October 1990
Collection mainly replicas of Egyptian pieces from several periods
Holds Tothmea, the only Egyptian mummy in Brazil, donated in 1995 by the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum in San Jose, California
